Throughout my research, I have played diverse roles in various projects, from leading conceptualization and execution to helping supervise students and securing funding. My first-author papers reflect my central involvement in writing, formal analysis, and project leadership. Open Access publication for papers during my time at the University of Bonn was made possible through funding organized by Projekt DEAL.

I led @whitney_probabilistic_2018 as part of the Competitive Research Grants for Innovative Methods and Metrics for Agriculture and Nutrition Actions (IMMANA), with funding secured by Prof. Dr. Eike Luedeling. I contributed to refining the proposal, planning, and executing the project. @whitney_decision_2018 marked my first post-PhD publication, supported by the World Agroforestry Centre (ICRAF) as a working paper, with parts later incorporated into @whitney_probabilistic_2018. In @whitney_decision_2023, I contributed as an adviser within the INTERFACES and LANUSYNCON projects, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF). I also helped Prof. Dr. Lisa Biber-Freudenberger secure funding for these initiatives. @whitney_balancing_2025 was a product of my leadership as the lead author, with support from CGIAR’s Water, Land, and Ecosystems (WLE) program (Grant No. D-0341) and environmental flow hydrology data provided by USAID.

As the last author on several papers, I primarily guided the conceptual direction, helped supervise research, and ensured strong research outputs. @do_decision_2020 stemmed from my work with an MSc student, where I provided significant input on R programming, research design, and conceptualization, alongside securing DAAD funding for fieldwork in Vietnam. Similarly, I conceptualized @tabuti_priority_2022, supported through the ENRECA project at Gulu University, assisting Prof. Dr. John Tabuti in securing funding and linking the work to my R package @whitney_ethnobotanyr_2021. In @luu_how_2024, I was deeply involved in modeling and writing and helped the lead author secure funding through the Schlumberger Foundation’s Faculty for the Future Program. For @netter_agroforestry_2022, I helped supervise the MSc student, performed formal analysis in R, formulated the models, and facilitated ASA program scholarship funding via the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

In my role as a middle author, I frequently contributed to conceptualization, programming, model development, and writing. In @kuyah_agroforestry_2019, I worked closely with the first author on assessment, statistics, and writing, assisting in securing funding from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation. My collaboration with AFLI and CIFOR-ICRAF Vietnam led to @do_adapting_2024, where I helped supervise the PhD student I had previously worked with during their MSc. The project was part of Can Agroforestry Contribute to Sustainable Development in Sloping Upland Areas of the Mekong Region? and received funding from the Academy for International Agricultural Research (ACINAR).

I was a key contributor to @mcgonigle_knowledge_2020, collaborating with CGIAR colleagues to secure WLE funding for sustainability research. In @kamau_holistic_2021, I helped supervise the PhD student, contributing to conceptualization and writing. My work in @lanzanova_improving_2019 extended to conceptualizing the project, leading fieldwork, and developing models, supported by CGIAR’s TAI research initiative in the Northern Volta River Basin. In @yigzaw_stochastic_2019, I helped supervise the PhD student and led model development in R, with funding from DAAD under the "A World Without Hunger" initiative.

My contributions to @oluoch_integrated_2022, @oluoch_indigenous_2023, and @oluoch_predicted_2024 included working with the PhD student, leading data analysis, and programming models in R. I also supported Prof. Dr. Christine Schmitt in securing BMZ-GIZ funding through FIA and assisted the student in obtaining a ‘Get Finished’ scholarship from the University of Bonn. Similarly, in @fernandez_prioritizing_2022, I led the project, worked closely on model development, and helped secure funding from GIZ’s ABNB initiative.

My role in @fernandez_prospects_2020 and @rojas_adapting_2021 involved helping supervise the graduate students who were the lead authors, guiding conceptualization, model development, and R programming, as well as assisting Prof. Dr. Luedeling in securing PASIT funding from BMBF. In @luu_decision_2022 and @luu_stakeholder_2024, I helped supervise the PhD student and contributed to model development, securing funding from the Schlumberger Foundation.

For @ruett_assessing_2022, @ruett_hyperspectral_2022, and @ruett_model-based_2020, I helped supervise the PhD student, contributed to conceptualization, and played a central role in model development and R programming. I also assisted Prof. Dr. Eike Luedeling in obtaining funding from Stiftung Zukunft NRW for the INRUGA project. Similarly, in @tamba_stochastic_2021, I helped supervise the student and played a major role in model development and R programming.

In @luedeling_limitations_2022, I contributed to the conceptualization and development of the manuscript in collaboration with the co-authors. My role included refining the methodological approach, reviewing key arguments, and ensuring the clarity of the final publication.

For @burbano-figueroa_profitability_2022 and @burbano-figueroa_farm-planning_2022, I was responsible for methodological contributions, particularly in structuring the analytical approach alongside the lead authors. Additionally, I played a role in data visualization and substantially revised the manuscripts, ensuring coherence in framing and interpretation.

My work extended to @liman_harou_mapping_2020 and @liman_harou_crop_2021, where I helped supervise the PhD student and contributed extensively to conceptualization, writing, and programming. For @sulaiman_socio-cultural_2021, I helped supervise the PhD student, contributed to conceptualization, and led model development in R, basing the analysis on my @whitney_ethnobotanyr_2021 package. I also led data analysis and model programming for @nyamukuru_allometric_2023, assisting the lead author in securing funding through the NORHED program (UGA-13/0019) under NORAD.
